taskOrMaterials: Provide an accessible familiar play/work opportunity, then leave the opening and a real choice to the learner. They initiate a relevant exchange with a peer, listen and respond, and repeat with a different peer or context. Merely answering an adult’s scripted introduction does not establish initiative.

The learner proposes a feasible activity that actually involves at least two children, considers the other child’s suggestion and begins the agreed activity. Adults can provide safe materials and communication access without supplying the idea itself.

In a genuine useful task, identify when help is needed, select an appropriate available person and ask clearly. Distinguish academic, practical and emotional support examples and explain why asking sensibly helps; permission to ask remains even after a first attempt fails.

Actually provide suitable practical help to another child, and offer comfort/kind encouragement when a genuine appropriate opportunity occurs. A supplied story may teach judgement but does not count as spontaneous real helping. Do not manufacture injury, distress or a missing object.

Sample both requesting and providing help, including the effect on the other person. Complete the existing kindness/vocabulary checks separately; a polite request does not by itself prove practical help or the whole empathy-word inventory.

taskOrMaterials: Bind the task to an actual locally suitable plant and a familiar animal already under a responsible adult’s care, with a checked species-specific care profile, permitted child role, hygiene/access arrangements and adult responsibility. Do not acquire an animal or keep wildlife captive merely to conduct assessment.

The learner actually carries out an appropriate recurring tending responsibility and checks the result: for example providing the checked amount of water to the selected plant or helping the responsible adult refresh a familiar animal’s water when safe. Record the actual task/period/support; generic good intentions or a picture-sort alone does not establish recurring care.

Check complete plant/animal need lists and a reasoned consequence of an unmet need through supplied reliable cases and existing observations. Never withhold an animal’s food, water, shelter or care; no harmful deprivation is required for this authoring protocol. Need knowledge alone does not establish tending.

Check the full minibeast operation separately with an adult-selected safe creature/observation method: careful handling where appropriate, return to a safe equivalent place near the find, and one accurate ecological reason. A brief returned minibeast observation alone does not establish the separate recurring-animal-care duty.

Use species-appropriate observable outcomes, not universal watering/light/germination formulas or claims that every plant depends on bees. Concern, reserve or changing enjoyment can coexist with responsible care.

Conduct an accessible actual local walk/observation in a supervised suitable place, using a checked local key. Name at least three observed plants and animals, describe a small habitat within the larger one and relate its actual conditions to an organism; do not promise a particular organism will be present.

Compare an actual second microhabitat and revise an initial expectation in light of real observations. No lifting heavy slabs, unsafe pond contact, handling stinging/unknown creatures, harmful sun exposure or forced contact is required.

Separately account for inherited whole claims using supplied accurate examples: three contrasting habitat conditions, needs-to-features reasoning and one real interdependence; living/dead/never-alive comparison with reasons; and meaningful use of the declared life-process concepts. Moving alone is not a life criterion, plant response is not human intention, and a material’s biological origin is distinguished from a currently living organism.

Curiosity, enjoyment and positive regard are contextual channels, not a compulsory smile or confidence score. Actual careful observation may coexist with fear/reserve; naming exotic species from memory does not establish local identification.
